newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Awaiting the budget barrage.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Awaiting the budget barrage.

text.p: *Semi-government bonds retained their offered tone causing spreads to show a widening bias against Treasury debt.
*State budgets due to come in a flurry in late April/May.

Australian semi government bonds retained their offered tone over the past week causing yields spreads to widen against Australian Treasury bonds, giving up some of the ground seen last month, traders said.

Yields were mixed as the short end of Australian debt curve generally rallied following last week's weak labour force report and in anticipation of a benign outcome to next week's March quarter CPI report.
While little tender supply expected to emerge on the semis market in the immediate future, the states will be facing a stampede of state budget announcements in the coming weeks.

"I think that there is a risk that they (the states) are not going to be as tight as they have been, rather than they are going to be tighter than people expect," said David Bassanese, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia.

"My impression is that the states have been pretty tight over the last couple of years and now they are probably loosening the reins a little. Their forward estimates are pretty substantial surpluses...so you may find that they are cut back a little," he added.
Western Australian kicked-off the budget season last week, and although this failed to make an impact on the market, budgets for the more populous states will be coming in fairly quick succession.
Victoria pencilled in for April 29, New South Wales on May 6 and Queensland on May 27, while South Australia is due on May 29. The Federal government budget is on May 13.
Meanwhile, the semis spread narrowing seen last month came in the wake of a series of positive comments on the states by the U.S. credit rating agencies.
Standard & Poor's is expected to finish its trawl of the states over the next couple of months having affirmed both New South Wales and Victoria last month.
